Minimum eventual gates include actual prepared dispatch and same-assertion old-dispatch control, old-processor PCM/state/readback equivalence, live gain/mute/matrix ramp and retarget commands, post-fader observations, repeated zero-allocation/free render with positive audit liveness, resources/realtime and supported qualification. ## What exists, and what #442 did not deliver

`PreparedBuiltinsSession::strip_bindings` (`crates/builtins-compiler/src/lib.rs:1528`) is the single nonbanked lowering path. Bank-claimed strips are consumed earlier; residual strips become three separate GraphNodeBindings. No-console owners are InputProcessor, FaderProcessor(FaderMuteBuiltins) and MatrixProcessor(MatrixBuiltins). Live owners are ConsoleInputProcessor, ConsoleFaderProcessor(FaderMuteRampBuiltins plus Consumer<TrackFaderRecord>) and ConsoleMatrixProcessor(MatrixBuiltins plus Consumer<TrackControlRecord>) at lines3060–3170. The fader is rebuilt from validated initial parameters when its live owner is prepared, not from the prepared-only #429 chain. Each live owner currently drains immediately before its own arithmetic.

The prepared session has #442's immutable control_delivery, but strip_bindings does not propagate it to either scalar owner. #442's owner fields and GraphPreparedBuiltinBankInfo cover banks only. Scalar selection must therefore first copy the existing declaration into both concrete live scalar owners during this lowering. This is a small local part of #443; no new host policy or queue prerequisite is required for serialized eligibility. Keep existing host wrappers/defaults Concurrent and WebEngine's existing dedicated declaration. Do not infer scalar eligibility from platform, absence of a bank, queue state or being tested on one thread.

`RuntimeParts::node_kind` (`crates/graph/src/runtime.rs:1556`) removes each binding into NodeKind::Bound. `build_op` at line2691 then attaches direct/aliased observers to the runtime op. Scalar `finish_unit` emits RuntimeUnit::Op; it never enters chain_for. `execute_op` at lines1135–1200 reduces inputs, invokes the bound processor, then the executor observes its output. A single undelayed input is a bit-preserving copy or no-op (`reduce_plane`, line90); it is not another gain/matrix operation. Scalar fallback is real independent execution, not a padded bank lane. Current comments expressly say scalar per-node processing has no bank mono-collapse dispatch: preserve this fact rather than claiming a scalar witness test earns bank collapse behavior.

## Proposed bounded graph transformation

Use only immediately consecutive plain scalar runtime/program ops for the SAME track's PostFader then PostMatrix, neither banked. Require the lowered graph's exact producer relationship, one undelayed non-sidechain input into matrix, sole readership of fader, no fader graph output and no direct or aliased post-fader observer. Reuse the substantive existing chains_into predicate over singleton op lists where its inputs are available; do not change bank chains_into or turn source-level track adjacency into a proof. Also require actual scalar owner types and both delivery declarations.

A minimal transformation can retain both graph ops, buffer assignments, liveness and observer placement: put a two-owner scalar composite at the fader binding and replace the matrix binding with the existing explicit identity representation. The composite performs both arithmetic stages on the first op's buffer; the second op retains its original single-input copy/no-op into its original output. Thus downstream post-matrix observers still execute at their original op boundary, and graph op accounting/buffer allocation need not be redesigned. Restrict to consecutive plain execution units so unrelated processors, errors or observers cannot be reordered around matrix execution. Require both original nonempty-input stage ops; do not apply source/fan-in-zero shortcuts. Decline before consuming either owner if any structural proof fails.

This is a recommended implementation shape, not yet a frozen graph mutation algorithm. Before assignment, source inspection must identify the exact bind-time point where singleton dataflow/observer eligibility is available before either binding is removed and freeze how the existing identity representation is installed. In particular, the identity substitution must not alter a buffer-sharing or observer alias proof merely because a processor disappears. Keep the original op schedule and reductions; no new scalar execution framework or arena API is needed.

## Traversals: the identity does not replace the removed arithmetic pass

Count loop sweeps separately from per-channel sample read/write coverage. For a settled pair of N frames, ignoring unchanged input-stage and outer graph work:

- Old fader executes TWO single-plane gain/mute loops: N left reads/stores and N right reads/stores. Old matrix executes ONE dual-plane loop: 2N reads and 2N stores. Total arithmetic: three loops, 4N scalar sample reads and 4N stores.
- New composite executes ONE dual-plane fader_matrix_block::<f32> loop: 2N reads and 2N stores, preserving exact gain/mute then matrix operands and identity selection. It removes the materialized faded intermediate from the arithmetic pipeline. Total arithmetic: one loop, 2N reads and 2N stores. These are source-level logical accesses, not generated machine instruction/traffic claims.
- The original graph's fader input reduction is unchanged. The matrix's single-input reduction is ALSO unchanged: either zero sample traversal when input buffer equals output, or two plane copies totaling 2N reads and 2N stores when distinct. No additional copy is introduced by changing Bound(matrix) to Identity.
- On a ramping call the composite retains the old three arithmetic loops (or their existing ramp/settled subloops) for the whole call, plus those same reductions. This is correctness fallback, not a settled-fusion claim.

The stable lowering already selects in-place output for a single undelayed sole-reader edge where neither end is dedicated (`program.rs:689–705`). `reduce_plane` checks that exact buffer equality and does nothing in that case (`runtime.rs:90–103`). Thus an eligible ordinary fader/matrix edge can retain TWO runtime op dispatches while its identity op traverses ZERO samples. Require the positive fixture to prove this current in-place case and the actual fused arithmetic dispatch. The claim must not be based merely on one fewer processor object.

If a legitimate selected edge has distinct buffers, the existing copy still traverses samples; that is residual graph placement cost, not an equivalent replacement for the removed arithmetic intermediate. Before: arithmetic4N plus copy2N reads/stores; after: arithmetic2N plus the same copy2N. Removing that residual copy would require an output redirect/liveness/observer proof and is not necessary to deliver the actual arithmetic fusion objective. Do not add it merely to remove the identity dispatch. A copy-free in-place positive demonstrates that this proposed scope is aligned with RT-4 rather than preserving all old memory passes under another name.

The record should say 'one settled scalar arithmetic traversal; original graph reductions retained', not 'one total traversal for every graph', and quote no speedup. Later #431 can measure a workload that actually selects this path. Ordinary control-queue reads/state writes are outside the PCM traversal count and remain mandatory.

## Concrete population proof

`crates/graph-compiler/src/schedule.rs:9–65` assigns each node one plus its maximum predecessor level, sorts nodes within levels, and returns ascending levels. `crates/graph/src/program.rs:531–550` enforces that the execution schedule is the concatenation of those levels. This is live single-thread scheduling; it is not the removed worker scheduler.

`crates/builtins-compiler/src/lib.rs:1946–1959` takes the real scalar route when `BankWidth::for_backend(dispatch)` is None, or when no planned banks exist. `into_graph_artifact` then calls `strip_bindings` (`1831–1893`), creating separate actual ConsoleFaderProcessor and ConsoleMatrixProcessor boxes and moving their separate queue consumers. The list's per-track insertion order does not override the graph's level-major execution order.

A concrete source-derived counterexample is two independent, same-depth tracks A and B, both lowered with Backend::Scalar, each with its ordinary unobserved sole-reader PostFader→PostMatrix edge, no sends/delays or other structural incompatibility, and BetweenRenderCalls ownership. At those two levels the real schedule is `F_A, F_B, M_A, M_B` in track/node-ID order. Neither matching pair is adjacent. Both have the same valid scalar dataflow and delivery population targeted by #443; no observer or Concurrent exemption explains their exclusion. Extra zero-work stages between earlier strip stages do not alter this final-level argument. This is a constructive source proof, not an executed fixture claim.

Runtime `units_of` and `build_sequential` (`runtime.rs:1782,1828–1861`) preserve plain scalar units; cohort runs merge bank membership, not these scalar owners. `finish_unit` at2791 returns a plain RuntimeUnit::Op for empty membership. Delivered #430's bank pairing therefore does not collapse the scalar counterexample or repair its scheduling. Current scalar lowering still lacks propagation of the immutable delivery declaration into its two concrete owners; #443 retains that approved task.

The existing proposed pre-build_op adjacent insertion remains appropriate for its bounded slice. It cannot be described as complete serialized scalar delivery. `execute_op` still invokes bound processors at their existing positions and propagates their errors. Eagerly moving M_A to F_A crosses F_B: if F_B fails, old M_A has not consumed its queue or changed state, whereas an eager pair has. Conversely delaying F_A until M_A would change already-completed fader state/queue effects before F_B fails. BetweenRenderCalls freezes producer admission; it does not make failures or state effects commute.
